new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager II - Laser Communications
new_jobs.description:
About Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we’re building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, laser communication terminals, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER II - LASER COMMUNICATIONS

Laser communication is the backbone of the constellations of today and tomorrow, and demand for it is growing fast. We are scaling industry-leading optical communication terminals to meet it: high-performing, affordable, and available at the volume commercial and government constellation operators need. Based at Rocket Lab’s global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, you are the customer’s champion and the delivery lead for our optical communication terminal programs. You own the customer outcome: the day-to-day relationship, delivery commitments and schedule at rate, milestone and acceptance reviews, risk, and program health. You build on a proven, standard terminal product and partner closely with our Product team on configuration, pricing, and new customer needs. You’ll work alongside the teams that build the spacecraft, the components, and the rockets, so the people you need to solve a problem are down the hall, not under another contract. This is a high-impact, customer-facing role: you connect the customer, our engineering teams, the production line, and the business across two continents, and you’re the person our customers count on.

What You’ll Get To Do

Lead Delivery: Lead terminal programs from award through qualification, production at rate, delivery, and on-orbit checkout, across current-generation production and next-generation variants. Hold each program to its plan and deliver on schedule, technical performance, and every customer commitment.
Lead the Team of Teams: Run multiple concurrent customer programs, work closely with Chief Engineers on link performance, data rate, SWaP, environmental qualification, and optical terminal interoperability, and dive in personally on the problems that matter most to delivery.
Deliver at Rate: Own each program’s delivery profile and protect it. Spot yield, supplier, and test-capacity risk early and drive it to closure with Operations and the Product team.
Forge the Supply Chain: Partner with Supply Chain to manage critical suppliers as strategic partners, building the relationships and accountability that keep every customer delivery on schedule.
Run the Program Lifecycle: Own program startup and baselining, milestone and qualification reviews, export and ITAR obligations with Trade Compliance, customer acceptance, and closeout across our U.S. and European sites.
Champion the Customer: Be the trusted point of contact for customers through milestone reviews, interoperability campaigns, acceptance, and delivery. Partner with BD & Strategy on proposals and with the Product team on pricing and configuration, bringing the voice of the customer to every decision.
Raise the Bar: Mentor the people around you, set a high standard for how we show up for customers, and help develop the program leaders who will run our next generation of laser communications programs.

QUALIFICATIONS YOU’LL BRING AS A SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER II

Engineering Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Physics, or Math.
Technical Depth: Working understanding of free-space optical or RF communications: link budgets, pointing, acquisition, and tracking, modems and coding, and space or airborne environmental qualification.
8+ years in space, aerospace, or photonics hardware programs, with multiple full program cycles. We weight the hardest thing you’ve shipped over the count.
Customer Delivery: A track record of leading a complex hardware program to delivery (customer, schedule, risk, and acceptance) and carrying it across the finish line under real pressure.
Production Delivery: Evidence you’ve moved real hardware from prototype to qualified, rate-production delivery to customers.
Program Financials: Experience managing program cost, EAC, and customer contract changes in partnership with finance and product teams on a program of meaningful scale.
Proof Point: You’ve delivered hardware at rate to a demanding customer and kept their trust through a hard moment, such as a slip, a test failure, or a contract change.
Clearance: U.S. Person status required (ITAR/EAR); ability to obtain a security clearance preferred.

These Qualifications Would Be Nice To Have

Domain Authority: Direct experience with optical inter-satellite links or optical ground or airborne terminals.
Production Velocity: A proven playbook for taking low-volume, hand-built optical or electro-optical hardware into high-rate production without sacrificing reliability.
Constellation Fluency: Experience delivering to large commercial or defense constellation programs.
Customer Leadership: Experience as the primary customer interface for constellation operators or satellite primes, from kickoff through acceptance.
Global Leadership: Experience leading program work across geographically dispersed sites, including export-control and dual-use compliance.
Advanced Technical Credibility: A Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Optics/Photonics, Physics, or a related field.
Systems & Toolchain Fluency: You speak systems engineering (trade studies, interface control, requirement integrity) and use Jira, Confluence, and ERP/MRP to keep program health visible at speed.
AI Fluency: You put AI tools to work in day-to-day program management, from schedule and risk analysis to status reporting and customer communications, so you and your team spend more time on the problems that matter.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base Pay Range (CA Only): $153,000 USD - $229,500 USD

What To Expect

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important Information

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality. For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

new_jobs.description:
About this position:
Information System Security Manager in Colorado Springs, CO

The Essential Duties and Responsibilities are intended to present a descriptive list of the range of duties performed for this position and are not intended to reflect all duties performed within the job. Other duties may be assigned. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform each essential duty. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

Applicants will be notified via email or phone within ten business days regarding application status.

This position is contingent upon award of contract.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Serve as the Information System Security Manager (ISSM) responsible for overseeing cybersecurity, information assurance, and Risk Management Framework (RMF) compliance for assigned information systems and programs.
Develop, implement, and manage the organization's cybersecurity program to ensure compliance with DoD, Intelligence Community (IC), Federal, and organizational requirements.
Lead RMF activities throughout the system lifecycle, including system categorization, control implementation, assessment, authorization, continuous monitoring, and risk management.
Oversee the preparation, maintenance, and submission of cybersecurity authorization packages, including System Security Plans (SSPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), Security Control Traceability Matrices (SCTMs), and Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms).
Advise Program Managers, Authorizing Officials (AOs), Information System Owners (ISOs), and senior leadership regarding cybersecurity risks and compliance requirements.
Manage vulnerability assessment, remediation, continuous monitoring, and cybersecurity risk mitigation efforts.
Ensure compliance with NIST, DoD, CNSSI, ICD, and organizational cybersecurity policies and directives.
Supervise and provide technical guidance to Information System Security Officers (ISSOs), Information System Security Engineers (ISSEs), System Administrators, and cybersecurity personnel.
Coordinate security testing, vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, audits, and inspections.
Review and approve system security configurations, architecture changes, software implementations, and security control modifications.
Oversee implementation of cybersecurity controls across classified and unclassified information systems.
Support incident response activities, cybersecurity investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action planning.
Develop cybersecurity policies, procedures, standards, and training programs.
Provide cybersecurity metrics, compliance reporting, and risk briefings to leadership and government customers.
Participate in Configuration Control Boards (CCBs), technical reviews, engineering working groups, and program management reviews.
Ensure all personnel operating information systems comply with security policies, training requirements, and acceptable use standards.

Required (Minimum Necessary) Qualifications

Education Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related technical field. Additional years of qualifying experience may be substituted for education requirements.
Minimum of 7 years of experience in cybersecurity, information assurance, information security, systems administration, systems engineering, or related technical disciplines.
Minimum of 3 years of experience serving in an ISSM, ISSO, cybersecurity lead, or comparable cybersecurity management role.
Experience implementing and managing the Risk Management Framework (RMF) for DoD or Federal information systems.
Experience developing and maintaining Authorization to Operate (ATO) packages and related cybersecurity documentation.
Experience overseeing vulnerability management, compliance assessments, and security control implementation.
Experience managing cybersecurity compliance requirements for classified and unclassified systems.
Experience leading teams and coordinating cybersecurity activities across multiple organizations.
Strong analytical, leadership, organizational, and communication skills.
Experience briefing cybersecurity risks to senior leadership and government stakeholders.
Must possess or be eligible to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, And Other Characteristics

Thorough knowledge of Risk Management Framework (RMF) processes and NIST cybersecurity standards.
In-depth understanding of NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-37, DoD Cybersecurity Policies, CNSSI requirements, and Intelligence Community directives.
Knowledge of system security architecture, network security, cloud security, virtualization, and enterprise cybersecurity operations.
Familiarity with vulnerability management, security assessments, auditing, and continuous monitoring programs.
Understanding of security engineering principles and lifecycle cybersecurity integration.
Knowledge of incident response, configuration management, and security operations processes.
Ability to analyze complex technical risks and communicate recommendations to leadership.
Strong documentation, policy development, and technical writing skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects, systems, and cybersecurity initiatives simultaneously.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, cybersecurity tools, compliance platforms, and security management systems.
Knowledge of organizational procedures and workflows – understanding how work moves through a company.
Basic knowledge of relevant technologies or tools – e.g., Microsoft 365, communication platforms, or industry‑standard software.
Knowledge of customer service practices – principles of providing quality service and managing inquiries professionally.
Knowledge of data privacy and confidentiality principles – awareness of proper handling of sensitive information.
Communication skills (written and verbal) – ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
Time management and prioritization – balancing multiple tasks and meeting deadlines.
Problem‑solving and critical thinking – analyzing issues and selecting appropriate solutions.
Interpersonal and teamwork skills – building rapport and collaborating effectively with others.
Attention to detail – producing accurate, error‑free work.

Preferred

Active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility or current TS/SCI clearance.
DoD 8570/8140 IAT Level III or IAM Level III certification requirements satisfied.
CISSP, CISM, CAP, CASP+, GSLC, SecurityX, or equivalent advanced cybersecurity certification.
Experience supporting Air Force, Space Force, Army, Navy, SOCOM, Intelligence Community, or other Federal Government environments.
Experience supporting classified information systems, SCI environments, and Special Access Programs (SAPs).
Experience managing cybersecurity programs supporting cloud environments such as Azure Government, AWS GovCloud, or hybrid architectures.
Knowledge of Zero Trust Architecture implementation and cybersecurity modernization initiatives.
Experience with ACAS, HBSS/ESS, Splunk, Microsoft Defender, eMASS, Xacta, or comparable cybersecurity platforms.
Experience supporting DevSecOps and secure software development initiatives.
Prior experience serving as an ISSM, Senior ISSO, Cybersecurity Manager, Cybersecurity Program Manager, or Security Architect.

Necessary Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. Employees must always maintain a constant state of mental alertness. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Must be able to sit and work at a computer workstation for extended periods (frequently).
Must be able to review, analyze, and approve technical cybersecurity documentation (frequently).
Must be able to communicate effectively during meetings, audits, inspections, and executive briefings (frequently).
Must be capable of conducting facility visits, cybersecurity inspections, and system reviews in secure environments (occasionally).
Must be able to lift up to 20 pounds of equipment, documentation, or related materials (occasionally).
Must be able to travel in support of cybersecurity assessments, inspections, and customer requirements (occasionally).

Work Environment

The work environmental characteristics described here are representative of those that must be borne by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the role. Employees must always maintain a constant state of situational awareness. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the

Physical Setting

Primarily performed in government facilities, secure operations centers, SCIFs, engineering environments, and office settings.
Work may occur in both classified and unclassified information system environments.
Frequent interaction with Authorizing Officials, Program Managers, engineers, cybersecurity professionals, contractors, and senior government leadership.

Schedule And Flexibility

Standard full-time schedule.
Occasional extended hours may be required to support cybersecurity incidents, inspections, accreditation efforts, system outages, vulnerability remediation activities, or mission requirements.
Flexibility required to support evolving cybersecurity threats and operational priorities.

Other Pertinent Work Details

Must maintain all required security clearances and access authorizations.
Position may require routine access to classified information up to the Top Secret/SCI level.
Requires compliance with all applicable cybersecurity, privacy, and security regulations.
May oversee multiple systems, networks, programs, and cybersecurity professionals simultaneously.
Requires exceptional integrity, leadership ability, discretion, and attention to detail.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position will have supervisory responsibilities.

DOT Covered/Safety-Sensitive Role Requirements

This position is not subject to federal requirements regarding Department of Transportation “safety-sensitive” functions.

Additional Qualifying Factors

As a condition of employment, you will be required to pass a pre-employment drug screening and have acceptable background check results. If applicable to the contract, you must also obtain and maintain the appropriate clearance levels required and must also be able to obtain access to military installations.

Shareholder Preference

BSNC gives hiring, promotion, training, and retention preference to BSNC shareholders, shareholder descendants and shareholder spouses who meet the minimum qualifications for the job.

Bering Straits Native Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any status protected by state or federal law, or any other basis prohibited by law.

new_jobs.title: Senior Security Manager, Amazon Vulnerability Management
new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Security's Vulnerability Management Service (AVMS) manages the entire vulnerability management (VM) program across Amazon’s retail business special teams, and AWS. AVMS operates at an unprecedented asset scale, as well as diversity of business lines ranging from Cloud, Health Care, Payments, Devices, Fulfillment, and even drones!

AVMS’s mission is to be Earth’s best VM team, keeping customers safe and enabling software teams to build cool new innovations securely. We are looking for a Senior Manager of Security Engineering to take on this mission and our scale to make a profound impact across Amazon and its external customers.

Are you interested in building and leading a focused top-notch security team responsible for securing

assets from IoT to Drones? Do you get excited about the challenge of harmonizing differentiated security objectives into common solutions and processes? Do you like to analyze, play with data, and innovate with AI? Are you excited about getting into deep details of how software, hardware, and devices work as well as how vulnerabilities impact them? If so, this role is for you! This role requires understanding how software is built, businesses operate, to scale processes, assess risk, and make deep data driven decisions to manage vulnerabilities. Further, this role requires an innovator that wants to change the status quo to improve outcomes for customers.

Key job responsibilities

As the Senior Security Manager in AVMS organization you will be responsible for the remediation operations, process, and management of security findings produced by Amazon Vulnerability Management Service (AVMS) team.

You will create vision, charters, mechanisms, processes, and solutions that ensure 100% of vulnerabilities that could impact Amazon customer’s are mitigated and remediated. You will work cross functionally across software teams you own and others to create security solutions for Amazon. You will work within and across multiple security organizations to drive outcomes. You will have an infectious desire for securing customers, and analyzing through data which actions need to be taken every day.

You will lead an innovative team of security practitioners to ensure security risk is mitigated and then ultimately removed from the Amazon environment.

A day in the life

Your work will be dynamic and impactful. You will start your day with metrics and insights that lead the direction of your teams daily execution. You’ll attend cross functional meetings and support sessions designed to resolve and prevent vulnerabilities from taking hold in the Amazon environment. Further, you’ll spend a portion of your time sitting with other peer security leaders to understand how you can shift your organization to help them achieve their goals of securing the latest and greatest Amazon products. Should it be required, if danger comes knocking, you will be there to have your teams jump in to protect our customers.

The majority of your creative time will be focused on scaling vulnerability management across differentiated technologies, businesses lines, and business objectives.

About The Team

The AVMS organization is an international team with sites covering Seattle, Austin, Sydney, New York, Arlington, and London. The team is a mix of security engineers, software engineers, and data roles chartered together to tackle the problem of high scale vulnerability management.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?

At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture

In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic Qualifications

10+ years of industry work with hands-on security engineering experience
10+ years of risk assessment and enabling organizations making security decisions experience
10+ years of team management and building (including coaching and mentoring) experience
10+ years of communicating technical concepts to a non-technical audience experience
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field
Experience communicating technical concepts to a non-technical audience
Experience with hands-on security engineering
Experience in risk assessment and enabling organizations to make security decisions
Experience in team management and building (including coaching and mentoring)

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of information security risk-based prioritization
Knowledge of information security technologies such as security design review, threat modeling, risk analysis, and software testing techniques
Experience applying threat modeling or other risk identification techniques or equivalent
Experience architecting, securing, and operating Amazon Web Services

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.

new_jobs.description:
For questions regarding this position, please contact the Recruiter listed in the Supplemental Information section.

About The Position

Riverside University Health System (RUHS) seeks candidates for an RUHS Compliance Program Manager position. This role supports the development, coordination, implementation, and oversight of RUHS corporate compliance programs and activities. The selected candidate will supervise support staff, ensure adherence to applicable regulations, and perform related duties as required. Current certification in Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC)
is strongly preferred.

Key Responsibilities Include

Supporting compliance with federal, state, and county laws and regulations, including HITECH.
Providing subject matter expertise on medical privacy and information security.
Overseeing staff and managing program activities as assigned.
Assisting in achieving compliance goals and strategic objectives.

The RUHS Compliance Program Manager is a journey-level manager classification reporting to the RUHS/County Compliance and Privacy Officer. Incumbents are expected to perform complex and increasingly responsible work with minimal supervision, contributing to the design, execution, and monitoring of effective compliance programs. This position is distinct from the RUHS/County Compliance and Privacy Officer, which entails broader responsibilities in directing and managing regulatory compliance programs.

This class has been deemed eligible for the Performance Recognition Plan as set forth under Article 3, Section 311(C) of the County Management Resolution. Program eligibility requires employees to be in a leadership position, manage other employees or programs, and have significant influence on the achievement of organizational objectives.

Why RUHS Medical Center?

Riverside University Health System-Medical Center is nationally recognized for its innovative, progressive care and is considered one of the top employers in the region. The 439-bed Medical Center is a designated Stroke Center, Level I Trauma Center, and home to the only Pediatric ICU in the area.

For more information about RUHS Medical Center, please visit ruhealth.org .

Examples Of Essential Duties

Perform audits to assess compliance with various laws, regulations, policies, and standards such as those related to healthcare fraud, waste and abuse, billing and coding, clinical documentation, privacy and information security, research and ethics; maintain a system of reporting that provides timely and relevant information of all aspects of compliance issues.
Participate in appropriate level of response, develop corrective action plans and conduct compliance investigations while maintaining confidentiality of information reported, as appropriate.
Evaluate departmental continuous readiness to achieve compliance in the areas of healthcare privacy and security; assist in the development and implementation of privacy policies, procedures and breach notification as necessary.
Develop and implement policies and procedures for filing and investigation of complaints related to HIPAA/HITECH Privacy, Breach Notification Rules and related County guidelines and procedures.
Develop and monitor policies and procedures that establish standards for ensuring patient privacy protections, including by providing guidance to individual employees and departments on the HIPAA Privacy Rule, as appropriate.
Document and retain all complaints received as required by HIPAA/HITECH; establish and maintain a mechanism for tracking and reporting the investigation and resolving such complaints.
Develop and administer training for RUHS staff to promote awareness of compliance to regulatory standards.
Provide guidance and assistance to departments on a variety of privacy and compliance auditing, and internal control matters; document findings and prepare reports.
Supervise, assign, review, and evaluate the work performed by staff; direct the day-to-day operations of support staff.

Minimum Qualifications

Education:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree, preferably with a major in business administration, public administration, public health nursing, finance, accounting, or a closely related field to the assignment. (A master's degree from an accredited college or university in any of the aforementioned majors is preferred.) Possession of current Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC) certification is preferred.

Experience:
Three years of professional, journey-level experience in healthcare compliance, which includes internal auditing experience and experience in the development and implementation of HIPAA and/or privacy compliance programs.

Knowledge of:
Information security; theory, principles and practices of general healthcare; governmental accounting, budgeting and auditing; HIPAA privacy and security rules and regulations; privacy laws, rules and regulations relating to information and security; federal, state and local codes, rules and regulations including healthcare fiscal operations; the methods of developing systems forms for various types of accounting records and reports; information systems and their application to accounting operations; the principles, methods and techniques of public administration, personnel and business office management; the principles and techniques of supervision.

Ability to:
Develop and implement compliance and auditing programs; apply legal and administrative compliance policies to hospital or health systems; analyze data, draw logical conclusions, conduct independent audits, reviews, and make evaluations to ensure compliance issues and concerns are appropriately evaluated, investigated and resolved; recommend effective courses of action; communicate effectively in oral and written form; establish and maintain effective working relationships; conduct independent systems analyses of complex business processes.

Angela Levinson/951-955-5562/alevinson@rivco.org

For spousal preference, and as applicable, the following documents: a copy of your marriage certificate, spouse's death certificate, a letter of spouse's disability and/or letter of service-related death (if available) from the U.S. Veteran's Administration. Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace
(NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

Honeywell Aerospace Products And Services Are Found On Aircraft Across Commercial Aviation, Defense And Space. We Operate Through Three Business Areas

Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft

Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying

In this role, you will impact the successful delivery of aerospace defense and space programs, contributing to national security and advancing Honeywell’s position as a leader in defense technologies.

Responsibilities

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead and manage defense munition programs ensuring alignment with customer requirements and business objectives.
Develop and implement program plans including scope, schedule, budget, and resource allocation.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive program execution and resolve issues proactively.
Monitor program performance metrics and ensure compliance with defense industry standards and regulations.
Provide leadership and guidance to program teams fostering a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.
Direct the work and approve resource requirements and program estimates while leading integrated program teams utilizing Integrated Product Delivery & Support (IPDS) Process. 
Generate and implement program plans and business requirements within approved budget and schedule constraints.  
Coordinate with various Customer Business Teams (CBTs) and Global Business Enterprise (GBE) to ensure their application programs are supported in terms of technical performance, schedule, and cost requirements 
Employ PM tools and development processes, including statement-of-work (SOW) or Line of Balance (LOB), work-breakdown- structure (WBS), basis-of-estimate (BOE)

YOU MUST HAVE

Minimum of 7 years of experience in program management within aerospace defense or related sectors.

Proven ability to develop and manage complex program plans including scheduling, budgeting, and resource allocation.
Experience with risk management and mitigation strategies specific to aerospace defense projects.
Proficiency in program management tools and methodologies applicable to defense and aerospace industries.

WE VALUE

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or related field.
Experience managing programs in aerospace defense and space sectors.
Strong leadership and decision-making skills with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.
Excellent problem-solving and analytical abilities tailored to complex defense projects.
Adaptability to dynamic environments and passion for continuous improvement and innovation.
7 years of experience or knowledge of the Aerospace industry specifically in navigation
Six Sigma Certification (Green Belt, Black Belt or Lean Manufacturing; nice to have) 
Strong communication (oral and written) and executive presentation skills 

This position requires Project Management Professional (PMP) or Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification, which certification of the two will be determined by the level of the position & meeting the minimum experience requirements of the certification. Candidates who do not currently hold the certification required for their position level must obtain the applicable certification within six (6) months of hire. new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Invesco

As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco.

What’s in it for you?

Our people are at the very core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including:
Flexible paid time off
Hybrid work schedule
401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution
Health & wellbeing benefits
Parental Leave benefits
Employee stock purchase plan

Job Description

Your Role

We are seeking a Senior Project Manager to lead complex, high-visibility initiatives that span multiple teams, business functions, technologies, and external partners. This role requires an experienced leader who can drive execution in ambiguous environments, establish structure where none exists, and influence decisions across all levels of the organization.

This individual will guide initiatives through business case development, funding approval, planning, execution, governance, operational transition, and benefits measurement. The successful candidate must be comfortable presenting options and tradeoffs, challenging assumptions, and driving accountability across stakeholders.

The ideal candidate has successfully led large-scale technology, security, risk, audit, or transformation projects involving multiple workstreams, significant budgets, executive visibility, and competing priorities.

Oversees, plans and implements special projects related to existing and new technology initiatives. Typically focuses on cost and efficiency related to long-term solutions.

You will be responsible for:

Strategic Project Leadership
Lead complex initiatives consisting of multiple interconnected workstreams, initiatives, and stakeholders.
Define project objectives, success criteria, roadmaps, milestones, and measurable business outcomes.
Establish governance structures and decision-making processes that enable effective execution.
Create clarity and alignment in environments with evolving priorities, requirements, and organizational dependencies.
Drive collaboration across business, technology, security, legal, compliance, finance, procurement, operations, and external partners.

Business Case Development and Planning
Develop business cases, funding requests, executive presentations, cost estimates, and benefits analyses.
Develop and maintain detailed project plans, schedules, milestones, and delivery timelines aligned to approved business objectives.
Partner with subject matter experts and leadership teams to validate assumptions, estimates, risks, and projected outcomes.

Project Execution and Delivery
Drive delivery across the project lifecycle, from inception through implementation and closeout.
Manage scope, schedule, quality, risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies, interlocks, and change activities.
Build and maintain project plans, work breakdown structures, critical paths, milestones, dependencies, and implementation plans.
Track actual effort and internal hours against approved estimates and planned allocations.
Identify schedule variances, resource constraints, risks, and issues
Coordinate activities across internal teams, external partners, and project stakeholders to ensure alignment on deliverables, timelines, and commitments.
Maintain project documentation, RAID logs, action items, decisions, accomplishments, upcoming deliverables, and status updates throughout the project lifecycle.

About The Job

Project Manager

NSF MSRI-1 Project

Position Summary

The Project Manager is responsible for managing all aspects of a National Science Foundation (NSF)-funded Mid-Scale Research Infrastructure (MSRI-1) project, including technical scope, cost, schedule, risk, and stakeholder engagement. Working in close collaboration with the Principal Investigator and the science and technical teams, the PM ensures that all project activities are planned and executed in alignment with NSF’s Research Infrastructure Guide (RIG), the approved Project Execution Plan (PEP), and award terms and conditions. The PM maintains the performance measurement baseline across cost, schedule, and scope through the project change control process; oversees risk identification and mitigation; and serves as a primary point of coordination among the institution, NSF program officers, sub-awardees, and other project stakeholders. The PM is accountable for the quality and timeliness of all project controls outputs, compliance reporting, and lifecycle documentation required to meet NSF oversight expectations throughout the full duration of the award.

Responsibilities

Project Leadership

Oversee the day-to-day operations of the project office.
Sets and maintains a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing team culture.
Directs and coordinates the project controls team.
Oversees recruitment, onboarding, and professional development of project staff.
Leads regular project team meetings, technical reviews, and schedule update sessions; prepares and distributes meeting minutes and action item logs.
Collaborates with University support services (e.g., Sponsored Projects Administration, Business Administration, Information Technology, and Human Resources) for smooth project operation.

Project Planning and Execution

Spearheads Project Execution Plan revisions, partnering with the PI and technical team to implement key revisions, including the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), contingency management, scope management, scheduling, and risk assessment sections.
Develops and oversees the project schedule, including milestones, activities, and assigned resources.
Oversees execution of the integrated project plan and monitors progress against scope, schedule, and milestones.
Manages cross-functional dependencies and competing priorities.
Leads planning for major reviews, milestones, and deliverables, including documentation of operational and technical requirements and interfaces.
Identifies and manages emerging risks, issues, and resource constraints, and is accountable for timely resolution of any items identified.

Stakeholder Engagement and Reporting

Serves as primary conduit between the PI, science and technical teams, and NSF program officers.
Manages activities and communications across the University, NSF, sub-awardees, partner institutions, and the science community.
Develops and delivers project status briefings and presentations for internal leadership, external stakeholders, and NSF.
Prepares and submits progress reports, including monthly project status reports, variance analyses, and other documentation required by NSF award terms.
Leads preparation for external reviews and oversight activities.\
Represents the project at workshops, reviews, conferences, and planning meetings, as appropriate.
Maintains strong relationships with strategic project stakeholders and partners.

Project Management and Control

Leads project budgeting, forecasting, and resource management.
Monitors and controls project scope, cost, and schedule against the approved Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB).
Manages the project change control process to maintain baseline integrity.
Leads Control Account Management (CAM) meetings and monitors project performance.
Reviews all project controls deliverables, including schedules, cost reports, and Earned Value Management (EVM) analyses, for quality, accuracy, and NSF compliance before distribution or submission.
Develops and manages the project Risk Register, including identifying, assessing, and mitigating project risks throughout the project lifecycle.
Maintains visibility of project risks, issues, assumptions, decisions, and action items.
Leads quality management across project deliverables and management processes.
Promotes continuous improvement of project management processes, tools, and practices.
Accountable for compliance with NSF policies, the Research Infrastructure Guide, and award terms and conditions.
Oversees Environmental, Health & Safety compliance.
Accountable for data management and compliance with cyber security requirements.

Other Duties as Assigned

Work Environment And Physical Requirements

Primarily office-based with extended computer use
Frequent communication and collaboration with team members
Domestic and international travel may be required

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, or related field and six (6) years of related work experience managing multi-million dollar projects and project teams. OR advanced degree plus at least four years of relevant experience

Preferred Qualifications

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the interpersonal and leadership ability to effectively interface with a team of scientists, engineers, and project stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain budgets and project schedules in accordance with best practices, including ability to create a WBS dictionary, activity sequencing, critical path methodology, and resource loading. Proficiency in MS Project or Primavera for project scheduling is preferred.
Experience managing a federally funded research project, including familiarity with federal award terms, reporting requirements, and sponsor oversight processes. Prior experience with NSF-funded projects preferred but not required.
Sufficient technical knowledge of the subject matter domain to engage credibly with scientists and engineers, identify technically driven project risks, and communicate effectively across disciplines. Domain knowledge in earth sciences, drilling, or related fields is ideal but comparable experience in a technically complex research environment is acceptable.
Skilled at recording and controlling changes to the performance baseline (cost, scope, and schedule).
Able to identify and align project needs to the science mission and goals.
Working knowledge of Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS) and how to use it as an integrated management tool for successful project planning and execution.
Demonstrates knowledge of principles, methods, and tools for risk management.

About The Department

The Department of Earth & Environmental Sciences is a vibrant interdisciplinary department whose faculty’s research ranges from paleoclimate to deep earth dynamics. The Department is in the School of Earth & Environmental Sciences (www.cse.umn.edu/esci) which also includes the Institute for Rock Magnetism, the Continental Scientific Drilling Coordination Facility, the Minnesota Geological Survey, and the Polar Geospatial Center. The majority of the School resides in John T. Tate Hall on the Minneapolis campus, with some labs on the St. Paul campus. Other affiliated research units at the University include the Saint Anthony Falls Laboratory, the Institute on the Environment, and the BioTechnology Institute.

Systems Planning and Analysis, Inc. (SPA) delivers high-impact, technical solutions to complex national security issues. With over 50 years of business expertise and consistent growth, we are known for continuous innovation for our government customers, in both the US and abroad. Program Manager – Strategic Initiatives
Location: Washington, DC
Schedule: Hybrid, with flexibility
Duration: 4-month contract, with potential for a longer-term opportunity
Target Start: Late November / Early December 2026

Position Overview
We are working with an organization seeking an experienced Program Manager to support high-priority strategic initiatives, executive-level projects, organizational governance, and cross-functional planning. This high-visibility role will partner closely with senior leadership and teams across the organization to coordinate complex initiatives, support decision-making, improve internal processes, and drive projects from planning through implementation.

A key focus will be supporting the organization's evolving approach to artificial intelligence, including governance and oversight processes, internal technology implementation, change management, and adoption initiatives. The Program Manager will also coordinate leadership and committee activities, contribute to policy and procedure development, and help connect priorities across departments.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, proactive, analytical, and comfortable operating with significant autonomy. They should be able to manage complex projects, anticipate challenges, exercise sound judgment, and communicate effectively with stakeholders ranging from project teams to executive leadership.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic Program and Project Management
Lead a portfolio of strategic and cross-functional initiatives from planning and design through implementation, evaluation, and closeout.
Develop project charters, work plans, timelines, milestones, dependencies, deliverables, and success measures.
Monitor project progress, identify risks and roadblocks, manage competing priorities, and proactively recommend solutions.
Provide strategic and analytical support to leadership on organizational priorities, business challenges, and key initiatives.
Conduct research, environmental scans, and analysis to evaluate options, tradeoffs, risks, and potential impacts.
Develop project tracking tools, dashboards, templates, and reporting processes to improve visibility and accountability.

AI Governance and Technology Implementation
Coordinate AI governance and oversight activities, including committee operations, meeting agendas, minutes, decisions, recommendations, and action-item tracking.
Support the review and progression of AI use cases through established governance and approval processes.
Coordinate leadership discussions, working groups, and documentation related to responsible AI use, organizational policies, and oversight.
Support the implementation and organizational rollout of AI-enabled tools, including communications, training coordination, FAQs, user resources, and stakeholder engagement.
Track implementation progress, adoption metrics, user feedback, outstanding issues, and follow-up actions.
Partner with technical teams responsible for system configuration, security, and implementation to ensure alignment between technical work, organizational priorities, and governance requirements.
Help identify opportunities to improve AI adoption, internal processes, and the effectiveness of technology initiatives.

Executive and Committee Support
Prepare executive-level presentations, briefing documents, decision memos, talking points, status reports, and meeting materials.
Coordinate leadership meetings and committee activities, including scheduling, agenda development, documentation, decision tracking, and follow-up.
Support board-related working groups and governance initiatives, including preparing materials and coordinating priorities and deliverables.
Facilitate communication between leadership, committees, and cross-functional teams to ensure alignment and timely information sharing.
Support annual and long-term planning activities, track strategic priorities, and prepare updates for leadership review.

Policy, Process Improvement, and Organizational Coordination
Support the development, review, documentation, and improvement of organizational policies, procedures, and workflows.
Identify opportunities to streamline processes, strengthen governance, clarify responsibilities, and improve operational efficiency.
Coordinate internal working groups and task forces focused on policy, planning, and organizational effectiveness.
Serve as a liaison across departments to connect related initiatives, clarify expectations, and maintain alignment on priorities.
Contribute to departmental planning, internal communications, and organization-wide initiatives as needed.
Document processes, decisions, and recommendations to support consistency, transparency, and effective execution.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field required; a master's degree in public health, public policy, public administration, health services, or a related discipline is preferred.
At least 6 years of progressively responsible experience in program management, project management, strategic planning, business operations, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience independently managing complex, cross-functional projects with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and high-level visibility.
Strong project management expertise, including work plans, timelines, deliverables, risk management, status reporting, and implementation tracking.
Experience preparing presentations, executive briefings, decision memos, and other polished written materials for senior leadership.
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to research complex issues, evaluate options, identify implications, and recommend practical solutions.
Proven ability to work autonomously, exercise sound judgment, anticipate challenges, and move initiatives forward without extensive day-to-day direction.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt messaging for audiences at different organizational levels.
Demonstrated ability to build relationships, facilitate meetings, and coordinate effectively across departments and stakeholder groups.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, and SharePoint, along with familiarity with project management and collaboration tools.
Exceptional organization, attention to detail, follow-through, and discretion when handling sensitive information.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience in healthcare, public health, health research, nonprofit, public policy, or public-sector environments.
A master's degree in public health, public administration, public policy, or a related field, particularly with an emphasis on systems thinking, organizational strategy, or policy.
Experience coordinating executive committees, board-related initiatives, governance workgroups, or leadership task forces.
Experience supporting AI governance, responsible AI use, technology implementation, organizational adoption, or change management.
Familiarity with policy and procedure development, organizational controls, or governance frameworks.
Experience coordinating organization-wide initiatives that require collaboration among leadership, communications, operations, and technical teams.
Technical AI expertise is not required. The priority is experience managing the strategy, governance, implementation, communications, and organizational considerations associated with complex initiatives.

Ideal Candidate Profile
The strongest candidate will be an independent, solutions-oriented program manager who can step into an active portfolio of initiatives and quickly establish priorities. They will bring strong organizational skills, sound judgment, critical thinking, and the confidence to work directly with senior leaders.
This person should be comfortable balancing detailed project coordination with broader strategic thinking, connecting the dots across departments, anticipating what comes next, and translating complex topics into clear plans and recommendations.

Additional Details

Flexible hybrid arrangement in Washington, DC.
Initial four-month contract, with the possibility of a longer-term opportunity depending on organizational needs and fit.
The team is hoping to bring someone on in late November or early December to allow for onboarding and knowledge transfer.
Candidates with experience in complex, mission-driven organizations and strong cross-functional project leadership skills are encouraged to apply.

Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental compliance professionals who play a leading role in air quality permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. As a member of the Environmental team, you will support environmental programs aimed at ensuring compliance with air quality regulations and standards in the Americas while also enabling AWS's growth around the world.

As an Air Program Manager, your primary focus will be serving as the air compliance subject matter expert (SME) across an Americas sub-region, providing programmatic oversight and ensuring alignment of compliance practices across all AWS data centers. You will build regional-level compliance infrastructure (frameworks, standards, tools, and visibility) and provide functional direction to the Regional Environmental Engineers (REEs) who execute compliance at their sites. You will work closely with the Environmental team, engineering, operations teams, vendors, and other partners to ensure consistent application of air quality compliance programs, particularly those related to Tier 4 compliant diesel generators. Your role will involve providing technical expertise on local, state, and federal air regulations and creating strategies for continuous improvement in air compliance management. As the team's air compliance SME, you will support REEs across the region to resolve complex air compliance challenges and drive environmental performance. You will also play a key role in standardizing incident response and reporting protocols related to air compliance events.

The successful candidate will have extensive knowledge of air compliance and regulatory requirements in North America, demonstrated ability to develop and standardize complex compliance systems across multiple jurisdictions, and proven experience leading air quality initiatives that drive environmental performance and sustainability. The ideal candidate will excel at providing strategic guidance while maintaining strong attention to technical details and have a track record of successfully collaborating with diverse stakeholders to implement environmental compliance programs at scale.

Key job responsibilities

Build and lead regional air quality compliance programs, providing standards and functional direction to in-region engineers across North and South America

new_jobs.title: Air Program Manager, AWS Environmental
new_jobs.description:
Description

Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental compliance professionals who play a leading role in air quality permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. As a member of the Environmental team, you will support environmental programs aimed at ensuring compliance with air quality regulations and standards in the Americas while also enabling AWS's growth around the world.

As an Air Program Manager, your primary focus will be serving as the air compliance subject matter expert (SME) across an Americas sub-region, providing programmatic oversight and ensuring alignment of compliance practices across all AWS data centers. You will build regional-level compliance infrastructure (frameworks, standards, tools, and visibility) and provide functional direction to the Regional Environmental Engineers (REEs) who execute compliance at their sites. You will work closely with the Environmental team, engineering, operations teams, vendors, and other partners to ensure consistent application of air quality compliance programs, particularly those related to Tier 4 compliant diesel generators. Your role will involve providing technical expertise on local, state, and federal air regulations and creating strategies for continuous improvement in air compliance management. As the team's air compliance SME, you will support REEs across the region to resolve complex air compliance challenges and drive environmental performance. You will also play a key role in standardizing incident response and reporting protocols related to air compliance events.

The successful candidate will have extensive knowledge of air compliance and regulatory requirements in North America, demonstrated ability to develop and standardize complex compliance systems across multiple jurisdictions, and proven experience leading air quality initiatives that drive environmental performance and sustainability. The ideal candidate will excel at providing strategic guidance while maintaining strong attention to technical details and have a track record of successfully collaborating with diverse stakeholders to implement environmental compliance programs at scale.

Key job responsibilities

Build and lead regional air quality compliance programs, providing standards and functional direction to in-region engineers across North and South America
Set and maintain the regional framework for compliance with federal, state, and local air quality regulations related to emergency backup power systems
Ensure compliance with EPA regulations including 40 CFR 60 Subpart IIII (Standards of Performance for Stationary Compression Ignition Internal Combustion Engines)
Develop and implement air quality monitoring programs and compliance tracking systems for permitted backup power generation (Tier 2/Tier 4 diesel generators, natural gas, etc)
Establish standardized emissions testing programs and protocols that engineers and testing firms execute at their sites
Provide technical guidance on air quality compliance requirements
Support emergency response planning related to air quality incidents
Collaborate with the air permitting team and in-region engineers to ensure operational compliance with existing permit conditions
Stay current with evolving air quality regulations and industry best practices for diesel generator management
Develop and deliver air quality compliance training for relevant staff
Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for air quality compliance

About The Team

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain, and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of increasing responsibilities in EHS or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations experience, or Bachelor's degree
5+ years with air permitting and/or compliance experience at local, state, federal levels

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing multiple projects and priorities across teams in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities
Experience developing and implementing environmental compliance programs including regulated waste, water, and air regulations in accordance with applicable laws
3+ years with engine specific regulations including 40 CFR 63 Subpart ZZZZ and 40 CFR 60 Subpart IIII

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Seeking a Financial Crimes Data Analyst SME who can help execute enterprise-wide risk assessments, analyze financial crimes risks, and synthesize complex information into executive-level recommendations. Looking for someone who can strengthen risk assessment reporting, regulatory readiness, and decision-making for senior compliance and business leadership. The team needs someone who can bridge the gap between business stakeholders and technology teams by translating financial crimes risk assessment requirements into actionable data solutions, while ensuring data quality, reporting accuracy, and successful Agile delivery. They are lacking analytical support to manage SQL-based data validation, requirements gathering, and product execution across risk assessment initiatives, therefore, seeking a talented Data Analyst to join our team in Baltimore, Maryland, on a hybrid contract-to-hire basis. You will support the GFC Risk Assessment Product Owner in defining and documenting data requirements. Your role will involve utilizing SQL and Excel to analyze data for risk assessments, reporting, and strategic initiatives, conducting quality assurance reviews, and drafting and managing JIRA stories and sprint activities.

Support the GFC Risk Assessment Product Owner in defining and documenting data requirements.
Utilize SQL and Excel to analyze data for risk assessments, reporting, and strategic initiatives.
Conduct quality assurance reviews on sourced and processed data.
Draft and manage JIRA stories, requirements, and sprint activities.
Partner with technology teams and stakeholders to support risk assessment products and workflows.

Must Have - Skills & Qualifications

5+ years of Financial Crimes Data SME experience with the ability to help execute enterprise-wide risk assessments, analyze financial crimes risks, and synthesize complex information into executive-level recommendations
5+ years of experience as a Data Analyst within financial services or banking environments.
Strong SQL skills with experience querying and analyzing large datasets.
Advanced Excel capabilities including pivot tables, lookup functions, charts, and VBA.
Experience gathering data requirements and supporting product owners throughout project lifecycles.
Knowledge of banking and securities products, services, and market participants.
Experience working in Agile delivery environments.
Strong project management and organizational skills.
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement abilities.
Ability to translate business needs into technical requirements.
Detail-oriented approach with strong analytical and critical thinking capabilities.

Work Environment

This role is situated in a highly collaborative, fast-paced financial services environment with enterprise-level visibility. You will work in an Agile, product-focused team structure with sprint-based delivery cycles, involving compliance, risk, and technology stakeholders. The position is data-intensive, supporting multiple risk assessment frameworks, with a strong emphasis on communication, analysis, and execution.

This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Baltimore, MD.

Pay And Benefits

Lead requirements discovery and analysis for ServiceNow Service Portal, Service Catalog, Workplace, ITSM, and related platform capabilities.

Ability to ramp up fast and operate in ambiguity — minimal hand-holding, proactive, works without detailed instructions
Strong communication across levels — can tailor messaging from working teams up to senior stakeholders
End-to-end XFN project/program management — drives cross-functional projects to completion independently (5+ yrs experience)

NICE TO HAVE SKILLS:
PMP certification (preferred, not required)
Consumer electronics industry experience (beneficial, not required)
Program/project management specifically in customer support operations — called out as "particularly valuable"

COMPANY:

Our client is a Fortune 500 multinational technology company headquartered in Menlo Park, CA.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Post Sales Operations (PSO) group is seeking a highly skilled and motivated Service Readiness Program Manager to join the Service Planning & Strategy team. The Post Sales Operations group oversees customer support operations for all products. The Service Readiness Program Manager has the responsibility to support organizational operations and service readiness as launches new cutting-edge products. The ideal candidate is skilled at leading projects end-to-end, cross-functional collaboration, and operational excellence in customer support and support readiness, as well as being able to navigate complex project landscapes and drive continuous improvements across the organization.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Manage End-to-end Programs: Lead end-to-end customer support program management activities for new product introductions, ensuring readiness of support operations prior to product launch.
Drive Project Execution: Develop and maintain comprehensive project plans, timelines, risk management strategies, and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to drive successful execution against goals.
Drive Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner cross-functionally with customer support, engineering, product management, sales, and other teams to align objectives, maintain launch schedules, and ensure timely delivery of milestones.
Use Data to Define Solutions: Advocate for customer-centric solutions by defining customer support requirements and leveraging data-driven customer and industry insights.
Resolve Risks: Identify risks and roadblocks to product launch, lead resolution efforts, and facilitate team collaboration to execute on action items efficiently.
Support Operational Processes: Support operational improvements and efficiencies across product support planning, design processes, and overall support capabilities.
Evaluate Program and Operational Performance: Establish metrics to evaluate program and operational performance, regularly communicate progress, and identify opportunities for enhancement and optimization.
Maintain Post-Launch Performance: Track product performance post-launch, implement lessons learned, and drive continuous process improvements for future product introductions.

QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration or related field.
5+ years of experience in program management, preferably in technology or consumer electronics sectors.
Proven track record in leading cross-functional teams and managing complex projects from concept to completion.
Strong understanding of post-sales operations and new product introduction processes.
Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to influence senior stakeholders and lead strategic initiatives.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
5+ years of experience in a program management role, with a demonstrated history of success in both new product introduction and after-market operations.
Experience in similar technology environments.
Certified Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification.
Experience with data analysis tools and methodologies to drive informed decision-making.

EXPERIENCE:
5+ Minimum Years of Experience
